materials.vertexShader: varying vec3 vNormal; varying vec3 vView; void main(){vec4 p=modelViewMatrix*vec4(position,1.0);vNormal=normalize(normalMatrix*normal);vView=-p.xyz;gl_Position=projectionMatrix*p;}
varying vec2 vUv; void main(){ vUv=uv; gl_Position=projectionMatrix*modelViewMatrix*vec4(position,1.0); }

userData.name: Barnard's Star
userData.units: Separate display scale: sqrt(R/R_sun); unknown radii are representative.

radius_solar.note: Interferometric radius adopted in Table 2; uncertainty is 0.001 solar radii.
radius_solar.note_tr: Tablo 2'de benimsenen girişimölçer yarıçapı; belirsizlik 0,001 Güneş yarıçapı.

teff_k.note: ESPRESSO spectroscopic model fit; different spectral analyses give different estimates.
teff_k.note_tr: ESPRESSO tayfına model uyumu; farklı tayf analizleri farklı tahminler verir.

rotation_period_days.note: Activity-model rotation estimate, not the animation speed.
rotation_period_days.note_tr: Etkinlik modelinden dönüş tahmini; animasyon hızı değildir.

NASA Chandra (2020) — GJ 699: X-ray and ultraviolet flares
sources.locator: 2019 Chandra and Hubble observations; France et al. 2020

sources.title: Alvarado-Gómez et al. (2019) — Breezing through the space environment of Barnard's Star b

caveats: The surface and plasma are not resolved images of Barnard's Star.
Changing the sky year changes space motion only, not its temperature or stellar age.
The 2019 wind study concerned an older planet candidate; no planet or planetary claim is used here.
